content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike of 5xx + timeouts against hosted inference gateway in us-west-2 starting 2026-03-15T09:07:36Z. Error pattern: intermittent 502/504 + upstream timeout (read timeout). Affected customers: multiple high-throughput tenants, support tickets incoming. Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.

sre-oncall (sam): I'm taking war room. I see elevated 5xx rate from the gateway between 09:07-09:15. Initial suspicion: backend inference pods not responding -> connection timeouts to runtime pool.

aj (support): We have 5 live tickets complaining about generation timeouts and 502s. One customer reports whole production route degraded; they saw retries from client which increased load.

maria (eng-runtime): Pulling logs for model-serving nodes in us-west-2. I see a pattern: kernel selection process hitting stalls on large-batch requests. There's a lot of "kv-cache miss" churn logged. Example: 
```
runtime[model-runner] ERROR select_kernel: kernel_init_timeout after 2500ms for model redwood-v1-16k
runtime[cache] WARN kv_cache_evicted prefix=abcd len=1024
```
Looks like memory pressure + long stalls in quantized kernels.

leo (infra): Network metrics look ok, but NLB target health shows many targets unhealthy for brief windows. Health checks returned 504s while pod metrics show high goroutine+thread wait.

sam: Can we repro locally? Maria, any reproducer or a request sample?

maria (eng-runtime): Got a sample payload from support (sanitized). Repro steps below; observed 502 within 4s in the gateway: 
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \  
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \  
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-16k","input":"<long prompt repeated 10x>","max_tokens":2048}'
```
Response: 502 Gateway Timeout. On runner logs the request sits waiting on `kernel_init` for ~3.5s then we hit gateway timeout.

aj (support): Customer mentioned they had a new client rollout which increased concurrent long-context requests ~3x at 09:05. Could be bursty traffic exposing a weakness.

devon (product): Did we recently change any circuit-breaker or health-check thresholds? Also any canary rolled for runtime?

leo (infra): No circuit-breaker change today. We did push a minor autoscaler tweak yesterday but it shouldn't affect current health-check thresholds.

ops-bot: Deploy event recorded: eng-runtime/service-redwood-runner v3.6.2 deployed to us-west-2 at 2026-03-14T22:40:11Z.

maria (eng-runtime): v3.6.2 included a quantized kernel fallback to improve latency, but there's one guard that increases kernel init time for cold paths. It may be racy under burst. I'm reverting that guard on a small canary to test.

sam: Mitigation plan: 1) throttle customer-side spike via emergency route rate-limit bump (lower tokens) 2) enable fallback routing to redwood-v1-8k variant for long requests 3) roll back v3.6.2 guard if canary repros. Who owns each?

aj (support): I can contact the customers and ask them to temporarily reduce concurrency. I'll also apply per-tenant short backoff suggestions in replies.

leo (infra): I'll create a temporary route policy to favor older model variants and reduce NLB health-check sensitivity to avoid flapping for short stalls. Making change now: `rbac: route/priority us-west-2:older-variants=1`

maria (eng-runtime): Starting canary rollback on 2 pods in us-west-2. Monitoring logs. If rollback stops the kernel_init_timeout, we'll roll forward rollback to all.

ops-bot: Canary rollback job started: rollback-job-2268003456-1.

(09:22) maria (eng-runtime): Canary pods back up, logs show much lower kernel_init latency. Early signal: error rate down 60% on those pods.

sam: Good. Leo, how's traffic after route policy?

leo (infra): After policy, traffic to v1-16k dropped ~40% and routed to v1-8k. Overall gateway 5xx rate dropped from 4.1% -> 1.2% in 5m. No NLB flapping now.

aj (support): Customers report improved behavior after our guidance and noticing fewer timeouts. Tickets still open but downgraded severity.

devon (product): Next: postmortem items: are we missing an autoscaling knob for kernel cold-starts? Also need better SLO for model kernel init time and a traffic shaping recommendation for customers when launching high-concurrency long-context workloads.

sam: Action items (temporary/triage):
- maria: complete full rollback of v3.6.2 guard in us-west-2 (owner: maria) — ETA 20m.
- leo: keep route policy active for 2 hours, then gradually remove if stable (owner: leo) — ETA monitor 2h.
- aj: notify affected customers with suggested throttling/backoff (owner: aj) — ETA 15m.
- sam: follow up with sales/CS for impacted accounts, open P0 postmortem doc (owner: sam) — ETA 30m.

maria (eng-runtime): Rolling full rollback now. Also adding additional telemetry for kernel_init_time and kv_cache_evictions to help dig deeper.

(09:40) ops-bot: Rollback completed across us-west-2.

maria (eng-runtime): Post-rollback metrics: gateway 5xx now down to 0.4%, median p95 generation latency reduced to pre-incident baseline. kv_cache_evictions still elevated but not cause of 5xx now. I'll open an RFC to address kv cache eviction patterns and memory footprint for quantized kernels.

sam: OK transition to post-incident mode. We should capture timeline, RCA, and long-term fixes. Quick RCA draft: root cause = quantized kernel guard in v3.6.2 introduced a slow cold-path kernel_init under bursty, high-concurrency long-context workloads. Symptom = increased kernel_init latency -> pod health-checks transiently fail + gateway 502/504, clients retried -> higher concurrency -> amplification.

devon (product): Long-term action items:
- Instrument kernel_init latency as an SLI + set alert at >500ms p99.
- Add canary test with synthetic long-context concurrency load during deploys for runtime.
- Guide/Docs: Recommended client-side concurrency/backoff patterns for large-context usage.
- Autoscaler: add warm-pool pre-initialized kernels for large models to avoid cold starts.

sam: Assign owners + deadlines:
- Maria: RFC + patch to kernel init path to remove racy guard and add warm pool (ETA 2 weeks).
- Leo: implement route-level graceful degradation policy + improved health-check tuning (ETA 3 days).
- Devon: Docs + customer guidance + canary plan (ETA 1 week).
- Aj: Customer outreach follow-up & write incident summary to affected accounts (ETA 24h).
- Sam: Postmortem writeup with timeline and severity / detection analysis (ETA 48h).

aj (support): I'll send a templated message to customers and include specific repros and suggested mitigations.

maria (eng-runtime): Attaching snippets we added to logs for follow-ups (sample log grep): 
```
# increased telemetry fields
kernel_init_time_ms=3563 model=redwood-v1-16k pod=p-23 kv_cache_evictions=12
```
I'll add these to structured logs and track in dashboards.

sam: Anything else live? If no, we'll close war room and move to postmortem. Good job triaging quickly. :thumbsup:

leo (infra): I'll leave the route policy in place for 2 hours but monitor closely. If any regression, reopen.

ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Recorded incident ID INC-2026-03-2268003456.

sam: Closing war room — transitioning to postmortem. Please add any extra notes to the postmortem doc.

maria (eng-runtime): Adding note: follow-up to test quantization fallback paths under concurrency; add perf tests in CI.

aj (support): I'll post a short customer-facing timeline in support tickets within the hour.

devon (product): I'll coordinate a scheduled postmortem review with eng-runtime + infra.

incident-bot: Reminder: follow-up task created: postmortem-INC-2026-03-2268003456 assigned to sam, due in 48h.
